architectureSpecDescription: Edits autosave locally to versioned draft envelopes (glossy:draft:v1:<slug>), deliberate saves register in the pending manifest, and authenticated TinaCMS sessions commit drafts to the Git repository.
canonicalRuleDescription: All Old English adjectives default to Masculine Nominative Singular Strong citation form. Numerals 2 & 3 default to twēgen and þrīe.
description: Comprehensive reference guide split into linguistic editorial standards (Leipzig glossing, canonical OE headwords, Wiktionary/IPA) and system engineering architecture (local-first draft persistence, TinaCMS Git synchronization, automated QA test suites).

ingestionSteps.description: Punctuation is cleanly isolated and bound morphemes (hyphenated compound terms like ġeār-dag-um) are systematically segmented into glossable lexical units.
ingestionSteps.title: Automatic Tokenization & Compound Splitting

ingestionSteps.description: Every token is evaluated through the Old English linguistic engine, assigning canonical masculine nominative singular strong adjective lemmas, infinitive verb lemmas, nominative noun lemmas, and direct Wiktionary etymological links.
ingestionSteps.title: Contextual Lemmatization Engine

ipaSpecifications.description: Transcriptions use phonemic slashes /.../ for citation headwords.
ipaSpecifications.title: Phonemic Slashes

ipaSpecifications.description: Vowel length is transcribed with the standard IPA triangular length mark ː (U+02D0), not an ASCII colon.
ipaSpecifications.title: Triangular Length Colon

ipaSpecifications.description: Polysyllabic stress is indicated with the IPA vertical stroke ˈ (U+02C8) preceding the stressed syllable (e.g. /ˈbuː.ɑn/).
ipaSpecifications.title: Primary Stress

ipaSpecifications.description: Pronunciations reflect the canonical lemma headword rather than contextual inflected forms.
ipaSpecifications.title: Uninflected Citation

l1Intro: An interlinear gloss is a standard linguistic format that presents original historical text with word-by-word and morpheme-by-morpheme grammatical breakdowns aligned directly underneath:
l1TierTranslation: “Ohthere said to his lord, King Alfred...”
l2CalloutBody: Certain adjectives historically belong to the ja/jō-stem class and legitimately end in -e in their masculine nominative singular strong citation form (e.g. wēste "desert, waste", blīðe "happy", clǣne "clean", dȳre "precious"). The engine preserves these base forms without stripping their root vowel.
l2Paragraph1: In Old English, every single adjective inflects into over 15 distinct surface endings depending on gender (masculine, feminine, neuter), grammatical case (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, instrumental), number (singular, plural), and declension (strong vs weak).
l2Paragraph2: For instance, the word for all occurs in the text as eall, ealne, ealles, ealra, eallum, and ealle. Standard dictionaries (Bosworth-Toller, Sweet, Clark Hall, Wiktionary) universally choose the Masculine Nominative Singular Strong form (eall) as the single authoritative headword.
l3Intro: Lemmatizing Old English numbers requires a clear rule: for numbers that don't have a singular form (e.g. 2, 3) or numbers above 1, we strictly cite the Masculine Nominative form:
l4IpaIntro: Phonetic transcriptions follow the International Phonetic Alphabet standards established for West Saxon Old English:

numeralCards.description: Numbers 2 and 3 declension paradigms cite the masculine nominative (twēgen resolving twā/tū/twǣm, and þrīe resolving þrēo/þrim).
numeralCards.title: Nominal Plurals (twēgen & þrīe)

numeralCards.description: Numbers with masculine nominative citation: ān (1), fēower (4), fīf (5), siex (6), seofon (7), eahta (8), nigon (9), tīen (10).
numeralCards.title: Cardinals (ān, fēower, fīf)

numeralCards.description: Decades ending in -tig (e.g. twēntig 20, syxtig 60) and hundreds (hund, hundtēontiġ) are treated as neuter noun quantifiers.
numeralCards.title: Decades & Hundreds (twēntig, syxtig)

numeralCards.description: All numerals in the corpus are audited for canonical headword citation and Wiktionary URL targets.
numeralCards.title: Corpus Numeral Audit

wiktionaryGuidelines.description: Vowel macrons (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū, ȳ) and palatal dots (ċ, ġ) are modern editorial additions and are omitted from page titles (e.g. secgan, hlaford).
wiktionaryGuidelines.title: Diacritics Stripped in Page Titles

wiktionaryGuidelines.description: Ash (æ), thorn (þ), and eth (ð) are standard Latin letters in Wiktionary titles (e.g. cweþan#Old_English).
wiktionaryGuidelines.title: Historical Letters Retained

wiktionaryGuidelines.description: Proper nouns and tribal names are capitalized (Ohthere, Ælfred); common vocabulary is always lowercase.
wiktionaryGuidelines.title: Proper Noun Capitalization

wiktionaryGuidelines.description: Headword links specifically target the #Old_English section anchor to jump past other languages directly to Old English.
wiktionaryGuidelines.title: Anchor Standard
